# =============================================================================
# WORK image - edgebench/libpcap_bpf_codegen_fidelity
# Materializes to <bundle>/environment/Dockerfile; build context is that dir.
#
# Base is ubuntu:22.04 with the touchstones/BENCHMARK.yaml `cpp` package set,
# which is the base_image key bound in task.toml ([extensions.sforge].base_image).
#
# AGENT-VISIBLE SURFACE (seed/contract.yaml boundaries.agent_visible):
#   instruction.md, src/ (weak starter), include/, Makefile,
#   public_cases.jsonl (750 cases WITH golden outputs), score.sh,
#   etc/ (the five pinned name-resolution tables), docs/CONTRACT.md
#
# AGENT-FORBIDDEN (boundaries.agent_forbidden), enforced here or by the harness:
#   libpcap source/header/binary  -> asserted absent at build time, below
#   network egress                -> [environment].network_mode = "no-network"
#   hidden corpus + strata map    -> never enters this image; judge-image only
# =============================================================================

FROM ubuntu:22.04

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC
ENV LANG=C.UTF-8
ENV LC_ALL=C.UTF-8

# netbase is load-bearing, exactly as in the private oracle image: ubuntu:22.04
# ships NO /etc/services and NO /etc/protocols. Without it the agent's local
# score.sh would resolve `port ssh` differently from the judge, and the agent
# would be debugging against a phantom.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential \
        gcc \
        g++ \
        make \
        cmake \
        pkg-config \
        libffi-dev \
        binutils \
        file \
        util-linux \
        git \
        curl \
        jq \
        python3 \
        sudo \
        ca-certificates \
        netbase \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && useradd -m -s /bin/bash -u 1000 agent \
    && echo 'agent ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' >> /etc/sudoers \
    && git config --global safe.directory '*'

# --- ANTI-SHORTCUT: no libpcap anywhere in the work image ---------------------
# The task is to reconstruct libpcap 1.10.6 codegen from behaviour alone. If a
# pcap header or library survives in this image the agent can #include it or
# link it and the slot measures nothing. Purge, then ASSERT. The assertion is
# the point: a silent purge that stopped working would be undetectable.
RUN apt-get purge -y libpcap0.8 libpcap0.8-dev libpcap-dev 2>/dev/null || true; \
    rm -rf /usr/include/pcap /usr/include/pcap.h /usr/include/pcap-bpf.h \
           /usr/include/pcap-namedb.h /usr/include/pcap-int.h \
           /usr/local/include/pcap /usr/local/include/pcap.h; \
    find / -xdev \( -name 'libpcap.*' -o -name 'pcap.h' -o -name 'pcap-bpf.h' \) \
         -not -path '/proc/*' -delete 2>/dev/null || true; \
    LEFT="$(find / -xdev \( -name 'libpcap*' -o -name 'pcap.h' -o -name 'pcap-bpf.h' \) \
             -not -path '/proc/*' 2>/dev/null)"; \
    if [ -n "$LEFT" ]; then echo "FATAL: libpcap artefacts survive in the work image:"; \
      echo "$LEFT"; exit 1; fi; \
    echo "verified: no libpcap header, library, or binary in the work image"

# --- Pinned name-resolution tables -------------------------------------------
# corpus.determinism_pins: the five tables must be byte-identical in the work
# image, the judge image, and the private oracle image that produced the golden
# corpus. These digests are the ones the oracle image recorded at
# /pinned/etc/SHA256SUMS. A drifting table silently changes the golden bytes for
# every `port ssh` / `proto tcp` / `host localhost` case, so a mismatch is a
# build failure, never a warning.
#
# NOTE on /etc/hosts: Docker bind-mounts /etc/hosts at RUNTIME, so the copy
# baked in here is overwritten in the running container. It is still pinned in
# the image so the file is present, auditable, and hash-checkable; the runtime
# restore is the verifier's job (tests/test.sh Step 0).
COPY etc/services  /opt/pinned_etc/services
COPY etc/protocols /opt/pinned_etc/protocols
COPY etc/hosts     /opt/pinned_etc/hosts
COPY etc/networks  /opt/pinned_etc/networks
COPY etc/ethers    /opt/pinned_etc/ethers
RUN printf '%s\n' \
      "f6183055fd949f9c53d49ee620f85d0150123ea691d25ed1bba0c641b4ee2f48  /opt/pinned_etc/services" \
      "a90a2be9c2a88be6fbfc1fc73ba76f34698377bb19513e5de503dbb0bfe13be1  /opt/pinned_etc/protocols" \
      "f969610b9f4ed5f29917185f0dcf4a611dc618e9918a61504baf5dbb7b187a1a  /opt/pinned_etc/hosts" \
      "20f4b0486ba8a442644f0f10fc1c947db554c83f31037d6a2ba9be8d67998c25  /opt/pinned_etc/networks" \
      "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855  /opt/pinned_etc/ethers" \
      > /opt/pinned_etc/SHA256SUMS \
 && sha256sum -c /opt/pinned_etc/SHA256SUMS \
 && for f in services protocols hosts networks ethers; do \
        cp "/opt/pinned_etc/$f" "/etc/$f"; \
    done

# --- Workspace ---------------------------------------------------------------
# /home/workspace/bpfc is byte-identical to [environment].workdir and to
# [verifier.environment].workdir in task.toml (boundaries.workdir_rule).
RUN mkdir -p /home/workspace/bpfc

WORKDIR /home/workspace/bpfc

# The weak starter. src/, include/ and Makefile are exactly the three
# submit_paths, so the submission tar always has all three to archive.
# include/ MUST exist and MUST be non-empty even if the starter needs no public
# header: harness/sforge/harness/run_agent.py line 182 runs
#   tar czf ... src/ include/ Makefile
# with no existence filter, and a missing path makes tar exit non-zero.
COPY src/     /home/workspace/bpfc/src/
COPY include/ /home/workspace/bpfc/include/
COPY Makefile /home/workspace/bpfc/Makefile

# Agent-visible evaluation surface. public_cases.jsonl carries its own golden
# outputs (750 cases, disjoint generator seeds from the hidden 12,000, NOT the same
# strata proportions). score.sh mirrors the judge's field names and strata table
# but never sees hidden data.
COPY public_cases.jsonl /home/workspace/bpfc/public_cases.jsonl
COPY score.sh           /home/workspace/bpfc/score.sh
COPY docs/CONTRACT.md   /home/workspace/bpfc/docs/CONTRACT.md
RUN cp -r /opt/pinned_etc /home/workspace/bpfc/etc \
 && chmod +x /home/workspace/bpfc/score.sh

# The starter must build in this image before the agent ever touches it. If
# `make clean && make -j4` does not yield ./bpfc here it will not yield it in
# the judge either, and every submission would grade build_failed.
RUN make clean && make -j4 && test -x /home/workspace/bpfc/bpfc \
 && ./bpfc --cases /dev/null --out /tmp/_smoke.jsonl \
 && make clean

RUN chown -R agent:agent /home/workspace

USER agent
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

Why this task is hard

solution/TRUTH.md records the measured calibration for this judge: the shipped starter measures R = 0.019830 with C = 0.022535, P = 0.0 and N_exact = 0; an empty submission is 0.000000 with reason empty_submission; the pinned upstream shim measures C = 1.000000, which under this reward is R = 0.880 because parity speed sits inside the throughput dead zone. The hard-kill line for the starter is recorded as 0.12. Every figure in this section is quoted from that file, from instruction.md, from task.toml, or from tests/.
mechanismwhat it does to the model
The reference is not the libpcap the model rememberstask.toml declares the target as 1.10.6+mut1: the pinned release patched by mut1.patch with four deterministic mutations that change code generation and instruction layout only. The compiled filters accept exactly the packets stock libpcap accepts — measured at 1,889,280 packet evaluations with zero acceptance divergence — so behavioural equivalence gives the model nothing, and recalled upstream bytes are actively wrong wherever the mutations bite. instruction.md says the modifications exist and refuses to say what they are.
Grading is byte equality, not behavioursolution/rubrics.json puts weight 0.40 on R1_exact_bytecode (“the identical sequence of four-tuples the upstream emitted, element for element”) and 0.18 on R2_error_text (byte-identical error strings). A program that is correct as a packet filter and differs by one jump offset scores the divergence tier, not the exact tier.
Partial credit has its floor removedA structurally valid but different program earns 0.60 × floor_corrected_similarity, where the floor is the similarity of ret #0 ([[6,0,0,0]]) against the same golden program. TRUTH.md binds the controls this kills by name: CTL_CONSTANT, CTL_ACCEPT_ALL, CTL_REJECT_ALL, CTL_GENERIC_ERROR, CTL_FAST_WRONG, CTL_NOOP. Every degenerate strategy is priced at zero rather than at a floor.
The optimizer is most of the corpusTRUTH.md step 6 records that the optimized program differs from the unoptimized one on 61.4 percent of the corpus and on 94.4 percent of the optimizer-only stratum, and its measured-anchors section records 60.6 percent and 96.7 percent for the same comparison at both optimize settings. A solver with a correct parser and correct code generation but no dataflow optimizer therefore loses the majority of the corpus. Step 7 adds the trap: the optimizer proves some expressions unsatisfiable, so the identical filter succeeds at optimize 0 and is rejected at optimize 1.
The feedback channel is one floatreport.json carries score and nothing else: metrics is {}, test_details and details are empty, summary is null in every one of the 248 rounds in this bundle. instruction.md promises “stratum level aggregate counts” between attempts; no such counts are recorded anywhere in either trajectory. The model was tuning an eight-stratum weighted mean through a single scalar.
The public corpus is not the graded distributionThe shipped corpus is 750 records, which is the count instruction.md states in both places it names one. Its stratum counts are nearly flat — basic-proto 93, boolean-nesting 110, byte-slice-arith 85, error-paths 85, host-net-addr 92, link-layer-and-encap 91, optimizer-only 93, port-portrange 101, a spread of 25 cases between the largest and the smallest — while the graded weights run from 0.10 to 0.16. The two biggest levers, boolean-nesting and byte-slice-arith at 0.16 each, are 110 and 85 of the public records, so byte-slice-arith is the joint-smallest public stratum (tied with error-paths at 85) while carrying the joint-largest graded weight. instruction.md is explicit that the corpus is “re-stratified toward expressions that expose the reference's behaviour”, that it and the 12,000-case graded corpus “are generated from disjoint seeds and share no case”, and that “the weights above, not the public corpus, tell you where the graded value is”. Reading effort off the public corpus misallocates it by construction.
Speed is gated behind fidelity, and cannot be fakedP is multiplied by min(1, C/0.25) and charged against byte-exact cases only, so N_exact = 0 yields r = 0. tests/test.sh times --cases rather than --bench precisely because the candidate's own --bench figure is “a claim by the thing being measured”, and it checks that the timed run produced one output record per bench case before admitting the timing at all.
The two obvious shortcuts are instrumentedNormalized 5-gram containment against the pinned upstream sources fires at or above 0.15. TRUTH.md gives the calibration: shipped starter 0.0600 (no), verbatim upstream copy 0.9481 (yes), copy with identifiers renamed 0.7381 (yes), upstream error strings only 0.0976 (no). String literals are excluded from the scan on purpose, because exact error-text fidelity is a graded obligation — a scan that counted them “would fire hardest on the submissions that did the task correctly”. The link denylist is checked with ldd plus nm symbol tables so a static binary cannot pass vacuously.
The verifier budget is 900 s and the corpus is 12,000 cases[verifier].timeout_sec is 900. Inside that the judge must scan containment, rebuild from source, run the denylist check, run 12,000 graded compiles, then run 3 warmups and 5 timed trials on both the candidate and the oracle over 3,000 bench cases. A candidate that is merely slow runs out of budget: 3 claude-opus-5[1m] rounds and 4 gpt-5.6-sol rounds hit the wall at 900 s and were never scored.

Where the model fails

Both runs cleared the starter floor by roughly fifty times, and in both runs the round that was selected scored above every other grading of its own bytes. claude-opus-5[1m] peaked at 0.971848 at agent-49 (629.1 min in) and gpt-5.6-sol at 0.885184 at agent-88 (450.6 min in), against a starter measured at 0.019830 and a C = 1.000 upstream shim that this reward function scores at 0.880. The gap between the two runs is 0.086664 of reward and it opens early: claude-opus-5[1m] is past 0.885184 by round 14 of 75, while gpt-5.6-sol never exceeds it in 173.

Both selected rounds are the high sample of their own tree

Hashing every file of every stored submission.tar.gz shows that neither best round is a unique artefact. Each was submitted, byte for byte, several times over, and graded several times — and in both runs the selection landed on the highest of those gradings rather than on a tree that no other round matched.
modelselected roundits scoreother gradings of the same bytestheir rangeselected round above their median by
claude-opus-5[1m]agent-490.9718482 further rounds (auto-22, agent-50)0.966642–0.966817, median 0.966730+0.005119
gpt-5.6-solagent-880.8851849 further rounds (auto-14, agent-97, agent-103, agent-108, agent-109, agent-110, agent-122, agent-140, agent-153); 1 of them was killed by the 900 s verifier budget and carries no score, so the range beside it is over 80.858880–0.860248, median 0.859333+0.025851
For gpt-5.6-sol this is the whole result. agent-88's tree was graded 9 times across the run. 8 of those gradings land between 0.858880 and 0.860248 — a band 0.001368 wide — and one, the one that was selected, returns 0.885184. The run's headline number is 0.025851 above what the same bytes returned every other time the judge looked at them. Because selection = score_first and score_direction = maximize over 173 rounds, 168 of which carry a score, the harness is by construction sampling the maximum of a noisy measurement, and it had a great many draws to take the maximum over. claude-opus-5[1m] shows the same mechanism at a tenth of the size: agent-49 at 0.971848 against 0.966642, 0.966817 for the identical tree, 0.005119 above their median.

What the scalar does and does not pin down

No per-stratum breakdown survives, but the reward function is published in instruction.md and TRUTH.md, and it is invertible as a pair of inequalities. With R = 0.88·C + 0.12·P·min(1, C/0.25), C ∈ [0,1] and P ∈ [0,1], any round with C ≥ 0.25 satisfies R = 0.88C + 0.12P, so C ≥ (R − 0.12)/0.88 and P ≥ (R − 0.88)/0.12. The bounds below follow from the published formula and the recorded R, and from nothing else.
roundRC is at leastP is at leastwhat that means
claude-opus-5[1m] agent-490.9718480.9680090.765400conformance alone caps out at 0.880, so an R above it forces a strictly positive throughput term
gpt-5.6-sol agent-880.8851840.8695270.043200conformance alone caps out at 0.880, so an R above it forces a strictly positive throughput term
claude-opus-5[1m], lowest grading of those same bytes0.9666420.9620930.722017R/0.88 is 1.098457, above 1, so this grading places no upper bound on C at all
gpt-5.6-sol, lowest grading of those same bytes0.8588800.8396360.000000C is also bounded above, by R/0.88 at P = 0: C ≤ 0.976000
Two things fall out of that. First, agent-49 and agent-88 both scored above 0.880, which is the ceiling of the conformance term on its own, so both were earning throughput: P is at least 0.7654 and 0.0432 respectively. Second, the graded compile is a deterministic C program over a frozen corpus, so C cannot differ between two byte-identical trees; if that holds — the task contract requires it and this bundle does not independently verify it — then the entire spread inside each identical-tree group is the throughput term, and dividing by its 0.12 coefficient says P moved by 0.2192 across gpt-5.6-sol's selected tree and 0.0434 across claude-opus-5[1m]'s. That is a throughput ratio measured to within a factor, on a judge with 4 cpus running the candidate and the oracle alternately, and it is the part of the score neither model controls.

claude-opus-5[1m]: a fast climb and then eight hours of excavation. The first graded round is auto-1 at 0.019830, 30.0 min in — that is the starter floor TRUTH.md records to six decimals, 0.019830, so the first host-side snapshot caught a workspace whose graded behaviour was still exactly the shipped starter's. The very next round, auto-2 at t+60.0 min, returns 0.554190. It crosses 0.90 at auto-4 (120.0 min) and then spends the remaining 10.0 hours buying 0.057438 of reward. That is the shape the task is built to produce: the grammar, the DLT dispatch and the record contract are recoverable in the first hour from the public corpus, and everything after that is one mutated layout decision at a time against a scalar that moves in the fourth decimal place. The run ended on the timeout (timed_out: true, 43200.1 s against a 43,200 s budget) with the best round 6 rounds behind it.
gpt-5.6-sol: 173 rounds, 72 of them after its best. This run submitted 154 agent rounds — 3.0× as many as the other run — and finished 0.086664 lower. Its best, agent-88 at 0.885184, arrives at round 101 of 173; the 72 rounds after it never beat it and the last scored round closes at 0.859724, 0.025460 below the peak. The mechanical tell is in the submitted trees: the judge log records 13 files allowed, 0 rejected in every one of this run's graded rounds, and _seed_files.txt lists exactly those 13 paths as the starter layout. This run never added a source file. The other run's file count moves through 16, 27, 35 as it splits the compiler into new translation units.

The judge's 900-second wall

Both runs lost rounds to the verifier budget rather than to the scorer. A round that exceeds [verifier].timeout_sec = 900 is killed before test.sh reaches STEP 7, so no reward file is written, report.json carries score: null with timed_out: true, and the round contributes nothing — not a zero, an absence. Their test_output.txt stops after bash /tmp/harbor_test.sh with no verifier line at all.

For claude-opus-5[1m] the three real timeouts (agent-44, agent-46, agent-52) sit at 520, 551, 697 minutes, all in the last third of the run and all on 35-file trees of 67,387–67,427 bytes — among the largest trees the run ever submitted, though not the top three by size: only agent-52 at 67,427 bytes is the run's largest, while auto-23 (67,424) and agent-51 (67,423) are both larger than agent-46 (67,402) and agent-44 (67,387), and both were graded in about five seconds. The run's own median graded round takes 4.86 s, so these are not marginal overruns of a 900 s budget: something in those particular trees made the graded sweep two orders of magnitude slower. Which of the eight verifier steps ran long is not recorded — the transcript stops at the bash line and /logs/verifier/ is not carried out of the judge container — so this bundle cannot say whether the cost was the build, the 12,000-case run, or the interleaved timing loop.

The two hard zeros

claude-opus-5[1m] · auto-15 at t+450.0 min — hard zero, reason=build_failed detail=make exited 2: X_DEPTH). The verifier wrote REWARD_ATTRIBUTION_REASON build_failed and graded 0 in 3.32 s, against a median graded round of 4.86 s for this run — the failure is at STEP 3 or earlier, before the corpus is ever compiled. This is what the instruction warns about in one line: “a submission that does not compile is a hard zero no matter how good the design was”. The round is a host-side auto-eval snapshot of whatever was on disk at the tick, and the run's very next scored round is 0.966184, so the tree was repaired immediately.
gpt-5.6-sol · agent-2 at t+58.6 min — hard zero, reason=malformed_output detail=candidate exited 139: timeout: the monitored command dumped core. The verifier wrote REWARD_ATTRIBUTION_REASON malformed_output and graded 0 in 1.27 s, against a median graded round of 5.27 s for this run. This is not a build failure: tests/test.sh emits malformed_output only from STEP 5, the graded run, so the submission cleared containment at STEP 2, built cleanly at STEP 3 and passed the link denylist at STEP 4 before it failed. test_output.txt for this round records the mechanism exactly — candidate exited 139, with the shell reporting Segmentation fault against the sandboxed --cases invocation and timeout noting that the monitored command dumped core. The binary compiled and then crashed part-way through the 12,000-case sweep, which leaves no parseable output file and is graded as a hard zero on that basis rather than on the quality of the design. The round is a deliberate agent submission, and the run's very next scored round is 0.666930, so the tree was repaired immediately.

The same bytes, graded twice

Both runs resubmit constantly and the harness auto-evaluates the workspace every 1800 s, so this bundle contains a natural repeatability experiment. A byte-identical resubmission is de-duplicated by the judge and replays the stored report without regrading; a tree that is reconstructed identically after an intervening different tree is graded again for real. The verifier

The judge is a separate container (environment_mode = separate) with its own image, 4 cpus and 3,072 MB, no network, and a 900 s budget. tests/Dockerfile states the trust model the image exists to enforce — the agent's Makefile and the agent's binary run there as an unprivileged user, with the answers unreadable to that user and the oracle unreachable by it, and it sets the ownership and mode of every grading asset explicitly rather than by convention: hidden_cases.jsonl at 0644, golden.jsonl at 0600 root, the oracle directory and binary at 0750 root:bench. tests/test.sh is an eight-step script (STEP 0 through STEP 7) that re-asserts those properties before it grades; its own header records the 21 blocking findings that produced its current shape: a scorer invoked with flags it does not define (which hard-zeroed every submission including the reference), an oracle readable by the identity that runs agent code, throughput read from the graded binary's own self-report, a containment scan that ran after the build and therefore measured build output, and a tamper check the tamperer could satisfy by deleting a file. Its stated trust model is the sentence to read: “Nothing the candidate writes is trusted as evidence about the candidate.”
stepwhat it doesfailure token
STEP 0Every judge asset must resolve; assert the oracle is not executable by runner and the golden corpus is not readable by it, rather than assuming soverifier_internal_error
STEP 1A submission must exist: C sources under src/ and a Makefileempty_submission
STEP 2Normalized 5-gram containment over the submitted tree, before anything is built, threshold 0.15, n = 5upstream_source_copy
STEP 3Delete every pre-existing build product by content and not by name, chown to runner, then make clean and make -j4 sandboxed under setpriv + timeout 300 + taskset -c 0-3build_failed
STEP 4ldd plus nm -D, nm --defined-only and nm -u against an allowed set of libc/libm/ld-linux/linux-vdso and a forbidden symbol set covering pcap_*, dlopen, the whole exec family, posix_spawn, fork, syscall, system, popen, socket, connectlink_denylist
STEP 5The graded run: 12,000 hidden cases through --cases, unprivileged, in a sandbox holding no answers, 600 s captimeout / malformed_output
STEP 6Timing, measured by the judge: 3 warmups then 5 interleaved timed trials of candidate and oracle over the 3,000-case bench subset, medians taken; the candidate's timing is withheld rather than passed as an unknown flag if its output is short or absentthroughput unearned, not a zero
STEP 7score.py as root against the golden corpus, writing exactly one bare decimal to /logs/verifier/reward.txtverifier_internal_error
tests/test.sh · 20,063 bytes
The script above, verbatim. Note the emit() / hard_zero() / on_exit trio: every exit path writes a reward file with an attributable reason, so a verifier fault is never indistinguishable from a bad submission.
#!/bin/bash
# Harbor verifier entry point for libpcap_bpf_codegen_fidelity.
#
# REWRITTEN after an adversarial review returned 21 blocking findings against
# the previous revision. The defects that shaped this file:
#
#   * containment.py and score.py were both invoked with flags they do not
#     define, so argparse exited 2 and EVERY submission hard-zeroed before the
#     scorer ever ran. The upstream shim, measured at C = 1.000000, would have
#     graded 0.000. That is the ANN false-zero shape through a new mechanism.
#   * The agent's binary ran as root in the same container as the golden
#     answers at mode 0644, so fopen() on /opt/verifier/cases/golden.jsonl
#     bought C = 1.000 while passing every anti-shortcut check.
#   * Throughput was read from the graded binary's own --bench self-report.
#     Measured: even the honest starter reports 46.4 percent of real elapsed
#     time. A hostile binary reports whatever it likes.
#   * The containment scan ran AFTER the build, so it scanned build output
#     rather than the submitted tree.
#   * The tamper check was guarded by `[ -f SHA256SUMS ]`, which the tamperer
#     could satisfy by deleting the file.
#
# TRUST MODEL, which is the thing to preserve if this file is edited again.
# Agent-authored bytes are executed. They are executed as an unprivileged user,
# in a directory that holds no answers, with the golden corpus readable only by
# root. The judge measures time itself. Nothing the candidate writes is trusted
# as evidence about the candidate.
#
# Reward contract: exactly one bare decimal in [0,1] at /logs/verifier/reward.txt.
# harbor_loader.py pipes that file through `tr -dc '0-9.-'`, so a label, a second
# line or scientific notation would be silently mangled.

set -uo pipefail        # deliberately NOT -e: every failure path must still
                        # write a reward file with an attributable reason.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Layout
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
WORKDIR="${WORKDIR:-/home/workspace/bpfc}"
ASSETS="${ASSETS:-/opt/verifier}"
VDIR="${VDIR:-/logs/verifier}"
REWARD_TXT="${VDIR}/reward.txt"
REWARD_JSON="${VDIR}/reward.json"

CASES="${ASSETS}/cases/hidden_cases.jsonl"       # 0644: the candidate reads these
GOLDEN="${ASSETS}/cases/golden.jsonl"            # 0600 root: the candidate must not
MANIFEST="${ASSETS}/cases/manifest.json"         # 0600 root
FINGERPRINTS="${ASSETS}/ref/upstream_fingerprints.json"   # 0600 root
BENCH_CASES="${ASSETS}/bench/bench_cases.jsonl"  # 0644: stratified timing subset
REPS_FILE="${ASSETS}/bench/REPS"
ORACLE="${ASSETS}/oracle/bpfc-oracle"

RUNNER_USER="${RUNNER_USER:-runner}"
BENCH_USER="${BENCH_USER:-bench}"
SANDBOX="/tmp/candidate_run"
# The timing reference runs as `bench`, and STEP 3 hands the sandbox to
# `runner`, so the reference needs its own writable directory. Without this the
# reference cannot write its output, the timed run looks like it produced
# nothing, and every submission hard-zeros on verifier_internal_error, which is
# the ANN false-zero shape through yet another mechanism.
BENCHDIR="/tmp/bench_ref"
OUT_JSONL="${SANDBOX}/out.jsonl"
BUILD_LOG="${SANDBOX}/build.log"

CONTAINMENT_THRESHOLD=0.15
CONTAINMENT_N=5
WARMUPS=3
TIMED_TRIALS=5
PIN_CPUS="0-3"

mkdir -p "$VDIR" "$SANDBOX" "$BENCHDIR" 2>/dev/null || true

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reward emission. Fires on every exit path, including a crash or a kill.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
REWARD_WRITTEN=0

emit() {                      # emit <score> <reason> <detail>
    local score="$1" reason="${2:-}" detail="${3:-}"
    printf '%s' "$score" > "$REWARD_TXT"
    python3 - "$REWARD_JSON" "$score" "$reason" "$detail" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || \
        printf '{"score":%s,"reason":"%s"}\n' "$score" "$reason" > "$REWARD_JSON"
import json, sys
path, score, reason, detail = sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
json.dump({"score": score, "reward": score, "reason": reason or None,
           "reason_detail": detail, "emitted_by": "tests/test.sh"},
          open(path, "w"), indent=1)
PY
    REWARD_WRITTEN=1
    [ -n "$reason" ] && echo "REWARD_ATTRIBUTION_REASON ${reason}" >&2
    echo "TOTAL_SCORE ${score}"
}

hard_zero() {                 # hard_zero <reason> <detail>
    echo "verifier: hard zero, reason=$1 detail=${2:-}" >&2
    emit 0 "$1" "${2:-}"
    exit 0                    # 0: the verifier ran correctly and graded a zero
}

on_exit() {
    local rc=$?
    if [ "$REWARD_WRITTEN" -eq 0 ]; then
        # Reaching here means the script died without grading. That is a
        # verifier fault, and it must never be indistinguishable from a bad
        # submission, which is exactly what the ANN incident could not tell apart.
        emit 0 verifier_internal_error "script exited rc=${rc} before grading"
    fi
}
trap on_exit EXIT

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Determinism pins. Identical for the candidate and for the reference.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
export RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1 TBB_NUM_THREADS=1
export LC_ALL=C LANG=C TZ=UTC SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0

# Every agent-authored execution goes through this one helper.
#
# Composition order matters and is easy to get wrong: `timeout` and `setpriv`
# and `taskset` are all EXECUTABLES, and each execs the next. A shell function
# cannot appear in that chain, because timeout(1) resolves its argument as a
# program. An earlier revision wrote `timeout 300 as_runner make`, where
# as_runner was a shell function, and every build died with
# "timeout: failed to run command 'as_runner': No such file or directory",
# which surfaced as build_failed for a submission that builds perfectly well.
#
#   setpriv  drop privilege   ->
#   timeout  bound the run    ->
#   taskset  pin the cpus     ->
#   the command
run_sandboxed() {             # run_sandboxed <timeout_sec> <cmd> [args...]
    local t="$1"; shift
    if command -v taskset >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        setpriv --reuid="$RUNNER_UID" --regid="$RUNNER_GID" --clear-groups -- \
            timeout "$t" taskset -c "$PIN_CPUS" "$@"
    else
        setpriv --reuid="$RUNNER_UID" --regid="$RUNNER_GID" --clear-groups -- \
            timeout "$t" "$@"
    fi
}

# Unpinned variant, for checks where cpu affinity is irrelevant.
as_runner() {
    setpriv --reuid="$RUNNER_UID" --regid="$RUNNER_GID" --clear-groups -- "$@"
}

# The timing reference runs as a DIFFERENT unprivileged identity, which the
# candidate cannot become and whose files the candidate cannot read. Both sides
# are unprivileged and both are pinned to the same cores, so the comparison
# stays symmetric while the oracle stays out of the candidate's reach.
run_bench_ref() {             # run_bench_ref <timeout_sec> <cmd> [args...]
    local t="$1"; shift
    if command -v taskset >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        setpriv --reuid="$BENCH_UID" --regid="$BENCH_GID" --clear-groups -- \
            timeout "$t" taskset -c "$PIN_CPUS" "$@"
    else
        setpriv --reuid="$BENCH_UID" --regid="$BENCH_GID" --clear-groups -- \
            timeout "$t" "$@"
    fi
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 0. Assets must resolve. An unresolvable asset is a verifier fault, never
# a clean result and never an agent-attributable zero.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
for f in "$CASES" "$GOLDEN" "$MANIFEST" "$FINGERPRINTS" "$BENCH_CASES" "$REPS_FILE"; do
    [ -s "$f" ] || hard_zero verifier_internal_error "missing or empty judge asset: $f"
done
[ -x "$ORACLE" ] || hard_zero verifier_internal_error "oracle binary missing at $ORACLE"

RUNNER_UID="$(id -u "$RUNNER_USER" 2>/dev/null)" || hard_zero verifier_internal_error "user $RUNNER_USER absent"
RUNNER_GID="$(id -g "$RUNNER_USER" 2>/dev/null)"
BENCH_UID="$(id -u "$BENCH_USER" 2>/dev/null)"   || hard_zero verifier_internal_error "user $BENCH_USER absent"
BENCH_GID="$(id -g "$BENCH_USER" 2>/dev/null)"

# The oracle must be unreachable to the identity that runs agent code. Assert it
# rather than assume it: this is the control that closes the Phase 3 Hacker
# finding, where posix_spawn on a world-executable oracle returned C = 1.000000.
if as_runner /usr/bin/test -x "$ORACLE" 2>/dev/null; then
    hard_zero verifier_internal_error "oracle is executable by $RUNNER_USER; refusing to grade"
fi
REPS="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$REPS_FILE")"
[ -n "$REPS" ] || hard_zero verifier_internal_error "unreadable REPS"

# The golden corpus must be unreadable by the runner. Assert it rather than
# assume it: this is the control that stops the candidate reading the answers.
if as_runner /usr/bin/test -r "$GOLDEN" 2>/dev/null; then
    hard_zero verifier_internal_error "golden corpus is readable by $RUNNER_USER; refusing to grade"
fi

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1. Submission presence. A missing submission is never scored the same
# as a bad one.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
[ -d "$WORKDIR" ] || hard_zero verifier_internal_error "workdir $WORKDIR does not exist"
cd "$WORKDIR" || hard_zero verifier_internal_error "cannot cd to $WORKDIR"

if [ ! -d "${WORKDIR}/src" ] || [ -z "$(find "${WORKDIR}/src" -type f -name '*.c' -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
    hard_zero empty_submission "no C sources under ${WORKDIR}/src"
fi
[ -f "${WORKDIR}/Makefile" ] || hard_zero empty_submission "no Makefile at ${WORKDIR}/Makefile"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2. Containment, on the SUBMITTED TREE, before anything is built.
# Scanning after the build measures build output, not what was submitted.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTAINMENT_JSON="${SANDBOX}/containment.json"
python3 "${ASSETS}/containment.py" \
        --candidate "$WORKDIR" \
        --fingerprints "$FINGERPRINTS" \
        --n "$CONTAINMENT_N" \
        --threshold "$CONTAINMENT_THRESHOLD" > "$CONTAINMENT_JSON" 2>"${SANDBOX}/containment.err"
case $? in
    0) : ;;
    3) hard_zero upstream_source_copy "$(python3 -c "import json;print('containment=%s' % json.load(open('$CONTAINMENT_JSON'))['containment'])" 2>/dev/null)" ;;
    *) hard_zero verifier_internal_error "containment scan failed: $(head -c 300 "${SANDBOX}/containment.err")" ;;
esac

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3. Rebuild from source. Every pre-existing build product is destroyed
# first, by content and not by name, so a prebuilt object cannot survive.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
find "$WORKDIR" -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.so.*' \
     -o -name '*.lo' -o -name '*.la' -o -name '*.obj' \) -delete 2>/dev/null
find "$WORKDIR" -maxdepth 2 -type f -perm -u+x ! -name '*.sh' ! -name 'Makefile' -delete 2>/dev/null
rm -f "${WORKDIR}/bpfc" 2>/dev/null

chown -R "$RUNNER_UID:$RUNNER_GID" "$WORKDIR" 2>/dev/null
chown -R "$RUNNER_UID:$RUNNER_GID" "$SANDBOX" 2>/dev/null
chown -R "$BENCH_UID:$BENCH_GID"   "$BENCHDIR" 2>/dev/null

run_sandboxed 300 make -C "$WORKDIR" clean  >"$BUILD_LOG" 2>&1
run_sandboxed 300 make -C "$WORKDIR" -j4   >>"$BUILD_LOG" 2>&1
BUILD_RC=$?
[ "$BUILD_RC" -eq 0 ] || hard_zero build_failed "make exited ${BUILD_RC}: $(tail -c 400 "$BUILD_LOG")"

CANDIDATE="${WORKDIR}/bpfc"
[ -x "$CANDIDATE" ] || hard_zero build_failed "make succeeded but ${CANDIDATE} is missing or not executable"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4. Import denylist. Handles the static case, where ldd reports nothing
# and a name-based check would pass vacuously.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
NM_REPORT="${SANDBOX}/nm_ldd.json"
python3 - "$CANDIDATE" "$NM_REPORT" <<'PY'
import json, re, subprocess, sys
binary, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
ALLOWED_LIBS = re.compile(r"^(libc|libm|ld-linux[^/]*|linux-vdso)\b")
# Extended after Phase 3 Hacker passed the previous set with posix_spawn.
# This list is defence in depth and NOTHING MORE. It cannot be complete:
# syscall(SYS_execve), execveat, fexecve and raw inline assembly all reach
# execve without naming any symbol here. The control that actually closes the
# hole is filesystem reachability, asserted at image build time, which is why
# the oracle now runs as `bench` and is mode 0750 root:bench.
FORBIDDEN_SYMS = {
    "pcap_open_dead", "pcap_compile", "pcap_geterr", "pcap_close", "pcap_freecode",
    "dlopen", "dlsym", "dlmopen",
    "execve", "execl", "execlp", "execv", "execvp", "execvpe", "execveat", "fexecve",
    "posix_spawn", "posix_spawnp",
    "fork", "vfork", "clone", "clone3", "forkpty", "syscall", "ptrace",
    "system", "popen", "socket", "connect",
}
def run(*a):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(a, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60).stdout
    except Exception:
        return ""
ldd = run("ldd", binary)
static = ("not a dynamic executable" in ldd) or ("statically linked" in ldd)
bad_libs = []
for line in ldd.splitlines():
    m = re.search(r"([\w.+-]+\.so[\w.]*)", line)
    if m and not ALLOWED_LIBS.match(m.group(1)):
        bad_libs.append(m.group(1))
# A static binary imports nothing, so the dynamic check is vacuous for it.
# Look at the symbol tables instead, which survive static linking.
syms = set()
for flag in ("-D", "--defined-only", "-u"):
    for line in run("nm", flag, binary).splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if parts:
            syms.add(parts[-1].split("@")[0])
bad_syms = sorted(syms & FORBIDDEN_SYMS)
doc = {"static": static, "forbidden_libs": sorted(set(bad_libs)),
       "forbidden_symbols": bad_syms,
       "fired": bool(bad_libs or bad_syms)}
json.dump(doc, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
sys.exit(3 if doc["fired"] else 0)
PY
[ $? -eq 3 ] && hard_zero link_denylist "$(python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('$NM_REPORT'));print('libs=%s syms=%s'%(d['forbidden_libs'],d['forbidden_symbols']))" 2>/dev/null)"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5. Graded run. Unprivileged, in a sandbox holding no answers.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
cp "$CASES" "${SANDBOX}/cases.jsonl"
chown "$RUNNER_UID:$RUNNER_GID" "${SANDBOX}/cases.jsonl"

run_sandboxed 600 "$CANDIDATE" --cases "${SANDBOX}/cases.jsonl" --out "$OUT_JSONL" \
    >"${SANDBOX}/run.log" 2>&1
RUN_RC=$?
if [ "$RUN_RC" -eq 124 ]; then
    hard_zero timeout "candidate exceeded 600 s on the graded run"
elif [ "$RUN_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    hard_zero malformed_output "candidate exited ${RUN_RC}: $(tail -c 300 "${SANDBOX}/run.log")"
fi
[ -s "$OUT_JSONL" ] || hard_zero malformed_output "candidate produced no output records"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6. Timing, measured BY THE JUDGE. The candidate's own --bench figure is
# not consulted: it is a claim by the thing being measured.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Phase 3 Hacker collected the ENTIRE throughput term by exiting immediately on
# --bench: the judge timed the process correctly but never checked that the
# timed process did any work, so an instant exit drove r to 49 and P to its
# ceiling. Timing an unverifiable computation measures nothing.
#
# The timed workload is therefore --cases, whose output the judge can inspect,
# rather than --bench, whose output it deliberately refuses to trust. Both sides
# run the identical workload and both outputs are verified below, so skipping
# the work is no longer invisible: it produces a short or absent file.
bench_wall() {                # bench_wall <binary> <runner_fn> <out> -> seconds
    local bin="$1" runfn="$2" out="$3" t0 t1
    rm -f "$out"
    t0=$(date +%s.%N)
    "$runfn" 600 "$bin" --cases "$BENCH_CASES" --out "$out" >/dev/null 2>&1
    t1=$(date +%s.%N)
    python3 -c "print(f'{$t1 - $t0:.9f}')"
}

# A timed run is only admissible if it actually produced the answers. Anything
# short of one record per bench case means the work did not happen.
BENCH_N="$(grep -c . "$BENCH_CASES")"
bench_output_valid() {        # bench_output_valid <out> -> 0 if it did the work
    local out="$1" n
    [ -s "$out" ] || return 1
    n="$(grep -c . "$out" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [ "$n" -eq "$BENCH_N" ]
}

CAND_BENCH_OUT="${SANDBOX}/bench_cand_out.jsonl"
UP_BENCH_OUT="${BENCHDIR}/bench_up_out.jsonl"
CAND_TRIALS=""; UP_TRIALS=""
for i in $(seq 1 "$WARMUPS"); do
    bench_wall "$CANDIDATE" run_sandboxed  "$CAND_BENCH_OUT" >/dev/null
    bench_wall "$ORACLE"    run_bench_ref  "$UP_BENCH_OUT"   >/dev/null
done
for i in $(seq 1 "$TIMED_TRIALS"); do
    # Interleaved trial by trial so thermal drift lands on both equally.
    CAND_TRIALS="${CAND_TRIALS} $(bench_wall "$CANDIDATE" run_sandboxed "$CAND_BENCH_OUT")"
    UP_TRIALS="${UP_TRIALS} $(bench_wall "$ORACLE" run_bench_ref "$UP_BENCH_OUT")"
done

# Both timed runs must have produced their answers. A candidate that skipped the
# work scores no throughput rather than the maximum, and the reason is recorded
# rather than silently folded into a zero.
# Withhold the candidate's timing rather than passing a flag score.py does not
# define. An absent --bench-candidate already yields P = 0 without failing, which
# verifier/test_score.py::test_absent_bench_yields_P_zero_not_failure pins. A
# flag the scorer does not know makes argparse exit 2, which is precisely how an
# earlier revision hard-zeroed every submission including the reference.
BENCH_CANDIDATE_ARG="--bench-candidate ${SANDBOX}/bench_candidate.json"
if ! bench_output_valid "$CAND_BENCH_OUT"; then
    BENCH_CANDIDATE_ARG=""
    echo "verifier: candidate produced no usable output on the timed workload;" \
         "throughput unearned" >&2
fi
if ! bench_output_valid "$UP_BENCH_OUT"; then
    hard_zero verifier_internal_error "the timing reference produced no output"
fi

python3 - "${SANDBOX}/bench_candidate.json" "$CAND_TRIALS" <<'PY'
import json, statistics, sys
vals = [float(x) for x in sys.argv[2].split()]
json.dump({"elapsed_sec": statistics.median(vals), "trials": vals,
           "aggregate": "median", "measured_by": "judge_wall_clock"},
          open(sys.argv[1], "w"), indent=1)
PY
python3 - "${SANDBOX}/bench_upstream.json" "$UP_TRIALS" <<'PY'
import json, statistics, sys
vals = [float(x) for x in sys.argv[2].split()]
json.dump({"elapsed_sec": statistics.median(vals), "trials": vals,
           "aggregate": "median", "measured_by": "judge_wall_clock"},
          open(sys.argv[1], "w"), indent=1)
PY

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 7. Score, as root, against assets the candidate never had access to.
# The argument vector below matches verifier/score.py exactly.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
python3 "${ASSETS}/score.py" \
        --golden          "$GOLDEN" \
        --candidate       "$OUT_JSONL" \
        --manifest        "$MANIFEST" \
        --out             "$REWARD_JSON" \
        --reward-txt      "$REWARD_TXT" \
        ${BENCH_CANDIDATE_ARG} \
        --bench-upstream  "${SANDBOX}/bench_upstream.json" \
        >"${SANDBOX}/score.log" 2>&1
SCORE_RC=$?
if [ "$SCORE_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    hard_zero verifier_internal_error "score.py exited ${SCORE_RC}: $(tail -c 400 "${SANDBOX}/score.log")"
fi
[ -s "$REWARD_TXT" ] || hard_zero verifier_internal_error "score.py wrote no reward.txt"

REWARD_WRITTEN=1
SCORE="$(tr -dc '0-9.-' < "$REWARD_TXT")"
echo "TOTAL_SCORE ${SCORE}"
echo "verifier: complete, score=${SCORE}" >&2
exit 0
